Yoda eventually completed the rest of the Force Priestesses' trials and was deemed worthy of learning the secret of eternal consciousness, and the beings instructed that Jinn would guide Yoda's training.<ref name="Sacrifice" />

Near the end of the war, Yoda was contacted by Dooku, who claimed that he was tired of the war and offered the Grand Master to come to [[Vjun/Legends|Vjun]] to discuss peace. Not trusting Dooku's intention, Yoda sought Jinn's counsel, entering deep meditation in order to feel Jinn's presence and hear his voice. Yoda asked if Jinn believed that Dooku was lying and was leading Yoda into a trap, and Jinn responded that that was what Dooku himself thought, but deep inside, Dooku actually wanted peace. Yoda did embark on the mission, but it did turn out to be a trap, and peace negotiations failed, although Yoda was able to escape from Dooku.<ref name="Dark Rendezvous">''[[Yoda: Dark Rendezvous]]''</ref> Throughout the final days of the war, in the moments when Yoda surrendered himself to the current of the Force, provided the current was calm, Yoda could sometimes hear the voice of Jinn, telling him that there was still much they needed to learn about the Force. However, Jinn believed that the secret of preserving one's consciousness would grant them great power.<ref name="LoE" />

During that period, Kenobi had dreams of Jinn still being alive, guiding him in that time of crisis. When he concentrated hard enough, he could almost hear Jinn telling him that until the possible became the actual, it was only a distraction, reminding himself to focus on the moment and give in to the Living Force. Shortly afterward, Skywalker was responsible for killing Dooku, bringing the Clone Wars close to an end. However, Darth Sidious, the true mastermind behind the Clone Wars, manipulated Skywalker's feelings for Amidala&mdash;who had become his secret wife and was pregnant from him&mdash;to lure him over to the dark side of the Force, proclaiming him Darth Vader and making him his new apprentice. Palpatine presented the Jedi Order as traitors, and issued [[Order 66/Legends|Order 66]] to the clone army, ordering them to kill their Jedi commanders. The Jedi Order was nearly wiped out, with Vader personally leading an attack on the Jedi Temple, slaughtering the younglings without remorse.<ref name="ROTS novel" />

Palpatine reorganized the Galactic Republic in the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], with himself as the Emperor, and a [[Great Jedi Purge/Legends|Great Jedi Purge]] began with the goal of exterminating the surviving Jedi. Yoda and Kenobi were among the few of those survivors, and they learned of Skywalker's fall. Kenobi followed his fallen apprentice to the volcanic world of [[Mustafar/Legends|Mustafar]], where they engaged in a climactic duel, which resulted in Skywalker losing most of his limbs and being heavily burned by the lava. Unable to deliver the final blow, Kenobi left Skywalker to die on Mustafar, but Palpatine was able to save Vader, outfitting him with a life-preserving cybernetic suit. Meanwhile, Yoda and Kenobi took shelter with Senator Bail Organa, who was still sympathetic to the Jedi. The Jedi brought Amidala to [[Polis Massa/Legends|Polis Massa]] so she could deliver. While Amidala was in labor, Yoda contemplated on the recent events, believing that he had failed the Jedi Order by being too rigid and old-fashioned, not accepting the change that was needed. Jinn spoke to the elderly Master, telling him not to blame himself and that Jinn would train him in the art of preserving one's consciousness. Acknowledging that Jinn had always been a great Jedi Master, Yoda pledged himself as Jinn's apprentice.<ref name="ROTS novel" />

====The dark times====
{{Quote|You're here." <br />"I have always been here. Being ready is your choice, my Padawan." <br />"But I do choose. I want to begin the training. I don't understand what you mean." <br />"When you know why you are not ready, you will be ready.|Qui-Gon Jinn contacts Obi-Wan Kenobi on Tatooine|<ref name="Last Jedi 1" />}}
Amidala soon gave birth to twins, [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke]] and [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia]], but died during childbirth. Hoping to protect the twins from the Sith, Kenobi and Yoda split them up. Organa agreed to adopt the girl and brought her to his home planet of Alderaan. On Yoda's advice, Kenobi was to bring Luke to the Lars family on Tatooine. Before Kenobi departed with the boy, Yoda informed him of his conversations with Jinn and taught Kenobi how to contact his former Master. Yoda exiled himself to the planet Dagobah, where he was being trained by Jinn,<ref name="ROTS novel" /> while Kenobi remained to watch over Luke on Tatooine, waiting for his first contact with Jinn.<ref name="Dark Lord">''[[Dark Lord: The Rise of Darth Vader]]''</ref> For months Kenobi waited until Jinn revealed himself, but to no avail. At that time, he reflected on Jinn's teachings, wondering if under Jinn's tutelage, Skywalker perhaps would not have fallen to the dark side.<ref name="Last One Standing">{{StoryCite|story=The Last One Standing|book=Legacy of the Jedi/Secrets of the Jedi omnibus|text=''Legacy of the Jedi/Secrets of the Jedi'' omnibus}}</ref>

Kenobi regularly meditated, talking to Jinn in his mind, despite the fact that the Jedi Master did not answer him. Kenobi told Jinn about his thoughts and feelings and spoke about the events that had transpired with him, most notably the encounters with the storekeeper [[Annileen Calwell]] and the entanglement with moisture farmer [[Orrin Gault]].<ref name="Kenobi novel">[[Kenobi (novel)|''Kenobi'']]</ref> When Tusken Raiders stole a large number of Lars' [[Moisture vaporator/Legends|moisture vaporators]], Kenobi went to the Tusken camp to retrieve the devices. Confronted by the Raiders, Kenobi had to engage them in battle, during which he started falling into a bloodthirsty frenzy, intent on killing all enemies, as he believed them responsible for Skywalker's fall since they had killed Shmi. However, Kenobi was stopped by a memory of Jinn in his mind, who told him to try to seek an alternative to murder. Instead, Kenobi simply unmasked his foes, which, according to Sand People customs, meant their defeat. Kenobi retrieved the vaporators and returned them to the Lars family.<ref name="Last One Standing" />

Not long thereafter, Kenobi was visiting the settlement of [[Mos Eisley/Legends|Mos Eisley]], where he heard a HoloNet report about Vader&mdash;whom Kenobi thought to be dead&mdash;[[Battle of Kashyyyk (19 BBY)|killing a number of Jedi]] on [[Kashyyyk/Legends|Kashyyyk]]. It was at that moment that Jinn contacted his apprentice for the first time. Initially surprised, Kenobi said that he should have finished Vader on Mustafar, but Jinn assured him that Anakin's future would be determined by the Force. Jinn assured his apprentice that Vader's painful memories of Tatooine would prevent him from looking for Luke there, but Kenobi was still supposed to look after him, making sure the boy did not discover who his father was.<ref name="Dark Lord" />

[[File:SWKenobi-coverart.jpg|thumb|left|225px|Jinn kept contact with Obi-Wan Kenobi during Kenobi's exile on Tatooine.]]
On Tatooine, Kenobi lived in a hut in the Jundland Wastes, and he started his personal journal, writing in it his experiences, including his adventures with Jinn.<ref name="Life and Legend" /> Vader himself, despite being immersed with the dark side, still retained some of his humanity and missed Jinn's guidance.<ref name="Lost Command 2">[[Darth Vader and the Lost Command 2|''Darth Vader and the Lost Command'' 2]]</ref> He would continue to reminisce on his time spent with Jinn and would remember the Jedi Master on multiple occasions.<ref name="Empire 1" /><ref name="Dark Times 2">[[Dark Times 2|''Dark Times'' 2]]</ref><ref name="Empire 4">[[Empire 4|''Empire'' 4]]</ref> Knowing that Amidala had died, and believing that their child had died with her, Vader had dreams of a potential existence in which he had not turned to the dark side and Amidala was still alive. In those dreams, Vader imagined them having a son named [[Jinn Skywalker]] in honor of Master Jinn.<ref name="Lost Command 2" />

A year after the rise of the Empire, Jinn kept in contact with Kenobi, but he refused to teach him the secret of immortality, believing that he was not ready. One day, Kenobi visited a cantina in Mos Eisley, where he overheard that a Jedi named [[Ferus Olin]] had survived Order 66 but was headed into the Empire's trap on the planet [[Bellassa/Legends|Bellassa]]. Kenobi walked outside his house and saw that his eopie had run away, and he started feeling angry. Jinn spoke to Kenobi, saying that it was not the eopie Kenobi was angered at, chiding his former Padawan for being unable to identify his feelings. Kenobi realized that he was angry at himself for being unable to make the decision to help Olin, believing that he was stuck on Tatooine having to watch over Luke. Jinn told Kenobi that Luke was not the only hope for the galaxy, and Olin could potentially become a valuable ally in the fight against the Empire. Jinn also felt that Olin would play a role in defeating a danger that threatened Luke's safety and informed Kenobi of his premonition. Knowing that Luke's life was relatively safe at the moment, Jinn promised to look over the boy, and Kenobi left Tatooine to help Olin.<ref name="Last Jedi 1" />

Kenobi helped Olin escape from Bellassa,<ref name="Last Jedi 1" /> also learning that Inquisitor [[Malorum]] had sent an [[Sancor|investigator]] to Polis Massa, the birthplace of the Skywalker twins, endangering the secret of their identity. While Olin traveled to Ilum to rescue another Jedi survivor, [[Garen Muln]], Kenobi felt that his mission required him to go to Polis Massa to protect Luke's identity. Jinn contacted Kenobi, urging him to trust his instincts. Kenobi prevented Malorum's investigator from learning the truth and then came back to extract Olin and Muln from Ilum. Even though Olin asked Kenobi to help him find other surviving Jedi, Kenobi returned to his duties as Skywalker's guardian on Tatooine instead. He finally realized that he had not been ready to learn Jinn's secret because he could not let go of the feeling of guilt for Skywalker's fall. Finally letting go of that feeling, Kenobi began studying the secret of eternal life from his master.<ref name="Last Jedi 2" /> [[17 BBY/Legends|Two years]] into his exile, an increase in Tusken Raider activity occurred on Tatooine, with the Sand People performing violent raids. During that time, Kenobi stumbled upon a destroyed Sand People camp, the same one which had been ravaged by Skywalker shortly before the Clone Wars. Jinn spoke to Kenobi, revealing that the massacre had been Skywalker's handiwork. When Kenobi asked Jinn why he had not told him about that earlier, Jinn enigmatically replied that Kenobi was not ready, although he did not specify what exactly he was not ready for. Before breaking contact, Jinn informed Kenobi that Skywalker had told few people about the massacre; one was Amidala, the other, Jedi Knight [[Darth Krayt|A'sharad Hett]]&mdash;the son of the late Sharad Hett&mdash;who had been raised by the Tuskens.<ref name="Life and Legend" />

Kenobi, who had initially believed that Hett had fallen victim to the Great Jedi Purge, eventually concluded that the man had survived. Indeed, Hett had returned to Tatooine, emerging as the leader of the Sand People and being responsible for the recent violent raids. Kenobi eventually confronted Hett, defeating him in lightsaber combat and severing one of his arms. According to the Tuskens' customs, the injury meant that Hett was an outcast among the Tuskens, and he was forced to leave Tatooine.<ref name="Life and Legend" /> At some point over the next seventeen years, Jinn finally shared his secrets with Kenobi, teaching him how to manifest himself as a spirit after death.<ref name="ANH">{{Film|IV}}</ref> Meanwhile, having himself mastered Jinn's teachings during his exile on Dagobah, Yoda was at one point visited by a fellow Jedi Purge survivor, Master [[Qu Rahn/Legends|Qu Rahn]]. Yoda passed Jinn's secret to Rahn, before sending him on the search for the fabled [[Vergence/Legends|Force nexus]] called the [[Valley of the Jedi]]<ref name="Dark Forces saga">{{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/article/sw20050407b|series=The Dark Forces Saga|text=Part 2: Unsung Heroes of the Light}}</ref>

====The prophecy fulfilled====
{{Quote|Your powers are weak, old man.''"<br />"''You can't win, Darth. If you strike me down, I shall become more powerful than you can possibly imagine.|Darth Vader and Obi-Wan Kenobi, just before the latter's death and return as a spirit|audio=YouCantWinDarth-ANH.flac|<ref name="ANH" />}}
During the Great Jedi Purge, Darth Vader discovered the son of the Jedi [[Kento Marek]] named [[Galen Marek|Galen]]. Sensing great Force-potential, Vader took Galen as his secret apprentice after killing the boy's father. In order to further the training of the boy&mdash;codenamed "Starkiller"&mdash;a prototype [[Holodroid/Legends|holodroid]] named [[PROXY]] was assigned to him. Programmed with a variety of training protocols, PROXY was able to assume the holographic form of a dangerous opponent, including several famous Jedi and Sith, using it to attack Starkiller at random points in time in order to keep his combat skills sharp. One of such programs was made to imitate Jinn and his mastery of Ataru. In [[2 BBY/Legends|2 BBY]], while possessed by the [[Core (Raxus Prime)|Core]], the planet-wide artificial consciousness of the planet [[Raxus Prime/Legends|Raxus Prime]], PROXY attacked Starkiller using the Jinn module, imitating Jinn's lightsaber style, with its swift efficient strikes and acrobatic movements. Starkiller defeated PROXY and freed him from the Core's control.<ref name="TFUn">[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed (novelization)|''Star Wars: The Force Unleashed'' novelization]]</ref>

When Starkiller visited the abandoned Jedi Temple as part of a [[Starkiller's Trial of the Spirit|vision quest]], he passed through the Temple's Planetarium. Although the Temple had been mostly ransacked during Operation: Knightfall and the years that followed, Jinn's statue in the Planetarium was still intact by that point.<ref name="TFU USE" /> Driven to the light side, Marek was later responsible for the creation of the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]], an organization that opposed the Galactic Empire's rule, beginning the conflict known as the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]].<ref name="TFUn" /> Leia Organa became one of the members of the Rebel Alliance, and in [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]] she attempted to secure Kenobi's help during the Alliance's efforts to stop the Empire's superweapon, the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station/Legends|Death Star]]. Confronting Vader aboard the Death Star, Kenobi gave his life to allow the nineteen-year old Luke Skywalker accompanying him to escape from the station with his friends. Having learned Jinn's secret, Kenobi knew that he would still be able to guide Skywalker from the afterlife. He indeed contacted Skywalker during the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]], helping him destroy the Death Star.<ref name="ANH" />

[[File:VaderLukeYodaKenobiJinn-SWGalaxySeries6.jpg|thumb|right|175px|The spirits of Jinn, Kenobi and Yoda bearing witness to Anakin Skywalker's death]]
By the time of the Galactic Civil War, two pieces of media mentioning Jinn were in circulation in the galaxy. One was a collection of five data-disks collectively called ''[[The Story of Count Dooku]]''. The documentary described the life of Jinn's Master in detail from the time of his apprenticeship to his death at the end of the Clone Wars. As Dooku's Padawan, Jinn was extensively mentioned in the work. During that period, a painting called [[The Phantom Menace (painting)|''The Phantom Menace'']] was available in the galaxy. The painting depicted the crucial figures in the Naboo conflict: Qui-Gon Jinn, Darth Maul, Obi-Wan Kenobi, Jar Jar Binks, R2-D2, protocol droid [[C-3PO/Legends|C-3PO]], Padmé Amidala and a young Anakin Skywalker, as well as a J-type 327 Nubian royal starship.<ref name="SWG">{{GalaxiesAED}}</ref> In [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]], Kenobi appeared to Luke Skywalker during the [[Battle of Hoth/Legends|Battle of Hoth]], guiding him to Dagobah and Yoda. After training with him for some time, Skywalker confronted Darth Vader on [[Cloud City/Legends|Cloud City]], discovering his heritage and narrowly escaping the fight, losing his hand in the process.<ref name="TESB">{{Film|V}}</ref>

Shortly after the confrontation, Luke returned to Tatooine, finding Kenobi's journal and learning of Qui-Gon Jinn and his training of Kenobi.<ref name="Life and Legend" /> [[4 ABY/Legends|The next year]], Skywalker returned to Dagobah in order to complete his training with Yoda. However, the Grand Master, who was 900-yeard-old, died of old age during Skywalker's visit. Taught by Jinn, Yoda's body disappeared and he became one with the Force. Shortly afterward, during the climactic Battle of Endor, Luke succeeded in redeeming his father aboard the [[Death Star II/Legends|second Death Star]]; Darth Vader was no more, and Anakin Skywalker<ref name="RotJ">{{Film|VI}}</ref>&mdash;remembering Jinn's faith in him as the Chosen One<ref name="ROTJ junior novel">[[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi (junior novelization)|''Star Wars'' Episode VI: ''Return of the Jedi'' junior novelization]]</ref>&mdash;turned on Palpatine, killing him to protect Luke from him, but sustaining fatal injuries in the process. With that sacrifice, Anakin had fulfilled the destiny Jinn had foreseen for him thirty-six-years ago and had brought balance to the Force.<ref name="RotJ" /> Jinn, Yoda and Kenobi were present in spiritual form during Anakin's final moments, witnessing his death in Luke's arms on the boarding ramp of a shuttle that Luke used to escape from the Death Star before its destruction.<ref name="Sketch">[[Star Wars Galaxy Magazine 6|''Star Wars Galaxy Magazine'' 6]] sketch card "Spectral Witness"</ref>

It was during that moment that Kenobi realized what Jinn had wanted to tell him so many years ago on Tatooine by saying he was not ready; Kenobi was not ready to forgive Anakin at that moment, but now, having witnessed his death, Kenobi set aside his feelings. Before Anakin's spirit could disappear into the netherworld of the Force, Kenobi reached out to him and taught him Jinn's technique, preserving his consciousness,<ref name="Life and Legend" /> thus allowing Anakin to appear alongside Kenobi and Yoda to Luke and his allies during the celebrations of Rebel Alliance victory over the Empire on the moon of Endor.<ref name="RotJ" /> [[5 ABY/Legends|A year later]], Master Qu Rahn was killed by the Dark Jedi [[Jerec (Inquisitor)|Jerec]]. However, having learned Jinn's secret from Yoda, Rahn successfully became one with the Force, guiding a Force-sensitive named [[Kyle Katarn]] in the fight against Jerec and his band of [[Seven Dark Jedi]].<ref name="DF II: JK">''[[Star Wars: Jedi Knight: Dark Forces II]]''</ref> Kenobi continued to be Luke Skywalker's spiritual guide for years, but he eventually moved on, saying the Skywalker was only the first of the new Jedi.<ref name="Heir">''[[Heir to the Empire]]''</ref>

In [[8 ABY/Legends|8 ABY]], Leia Organa and her husband [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]] visited Tatooine on a mission for the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]], the Rebel Alliance's successor state that had replaced the Galactic Empire as the galaxy's dominant government. During the mission, the two discovered a holojournal kept by Shmi Skywalker and met many witnesses of the events forty years before. From those sources, Organa learned about her father's origins and Jinn's role in his discovery.<ref name="Tatooine Ghost" /> Shortly after that, Luke Skywalker was responsible for creating the [[New Jedi Order]], and he also studied Kenobi's career closely, discovering many facts about Qui-Gon Jinn, such as his close friendship with Plo Koon.<ref name="Outcast">''[[Fate of the Jedi: Outcast]]''</ref> In [[40 ABY/Legends|40 ABY]], the son of Leia Organa Solo, [[Darth Caedus|Jacen Solo]], [[Flow-walking|flow-walked]] to the time when Jinn brought Anakin Skywalker to the Jedi Temple, overhearing the Jedi Council's debate regarding the boy's fate, hearing them saying that Jinn believed the boy to be the Chosen One.<ref name="Bloodlines">''[[Legacy of the Force: Bloodlines]]''</ref> Later that year, a member of Skywalker's New Jedi Order, Jedi historian [[Tionne Solusar]] featured Jinn in her work ''[[Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force]]'', focused on the history of the conflict between the Jedi and their sworn enemies, the Sith.<ref name="JvS" />

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|Qui-Gon Jinn was perhaps the greatest Jedi alive, a commanding presence at Council, a strong and brave warrior who refused to be intimidated by even the most daunting challenge, and a good and kind man.|Obi-Wan Kenobi|<ref name="TPM novel" />}}
[[File:Anakin_Obiwan_Quigon.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Qui-Gon Jinn's defiant personality made him insist on the recruitment of Anakin Skywalker to the Jedi Order.]]

Regarded as a maverick by his peers, Qui-Gon Jinn was a wise and faithful&mdash;but unorthodox&mdash;member of the Jedi Order. He was also a powerful warrior.<ref name="OW guide">[[Star Wars: Obi-Wan: Prima's Official Strategy Guide|''Star Wars: Obi-Wan'': Prima's Official Strategy Guide]]</ref> Jinn was a proponent of the Living Force concept, and his many attempts to help lesser creatures annoyed his master, Dooku, to no end. Dooku, Jinn, Kenobi, and Skywalker formed a chain of Jedi Masters and Padawans through which passed an independent streak, making them a difficulty in the eyes of the Jedi Council. Indeed, his Padawan Kenobi suggested that the Council would have invited Jinn to join them, if he would follow the Jedi Code. A distinguished and adept Jedi warrior, Qui-Gon Jinn reflected strength and wisdom.<ref name="The Phantom Menace" />

Qui-Gon came into knighthood during an era in which the Jedi Order was more conservative and committed to a democratic Republic. His commitment to studying the galaxy and interacting with it would prove far-reaching, having a great impact on Kenobi and his Padawan Anakin Skywalker, both of whom would greatly influence the founder of the [[New Jedi Order]], Luke Skywalker.

Qui-Gon was also known for his often-overwhelming compassion for all life forms. This commiseration led to his saving Jar Jar Binks from his punishment at the hands of his fellow Gungans, and contributed greatly to his freeing of Skywalker.<ref name="The Phantom Menace" />

Controversially, Jedi Master Qui-Gon Jinn was thought of as a [[Gray Jedi]] by some members of the Order for his frequent opposition to their demands.<ref name="Stark Hyperspace War 1" /> While the term was used to refer to Force-users who walked the line between light and dark, Jedi were also labeled as Gray Jedi for distancing themselves from the Jedi High Council. This practice dated back to the days of the Old Republic, when the High Council was attempting to consolidate power. Jedi who frequently clashed with the will of the Council were sometimes thought of as Gray even if they did not necessarily walk the line between the light and dark sides of the Force.<ref name="The Jedi Path" /> Despite this, he was a great teacher and mentor, and taught Kenobi the [[Nelvaanian/Legends|Nelvaanian]] tongue on their journeys across the galaxy, as well as others.<ref name="SWCW23">{{CW|23}}</ref>

The Jedi Master appeared much younger than his age and had a penetrating gaze. He also had a subtle attention to detail, seen as he could sense mood changes in the people around him and was quite adept at hiding his emotions from other individuals, even other Jedi. His master was often perplexed by his ability to do this even when Qui-Gon was a Padawan. He was also open about his opinions to the point of near-tactlessness, and his master Dooku once referred to him as a "solitary and secretive rogue."<ref name="Darth Plagueis" />

Jinn considered caring for one's physical appearance a futility. However, his looks and behavior were not unanimously approved within the Jedi order. Although he admittedly revered his colleague, Jedi Master Tholme once commented that Qui-Gon Jinn looked neglected "like a [[Bantha/Legends|Bantha]]" and exhaled a foul body odor reminiscent of that of a Rodian. Tholme also criticized Jinn for taking "every word" from his own mouth as a pearl of wisdom.<ref name="Stark Hyperspace War 3" />

As a ghost, he had a wide, if rare, commentary on the state of the galaxy, telling Obi-Wan advice such as to not tell Luke that Vader was his father, warning Kenobi about A'Sharad Hett's warmongering.<ref name="Life and Legend" /> 

==Powers and abilities==
===Lightsaber combat===
{{Quote|The perfect attack begins with your attention. Every pebble can be an obstacle or an opportunity. Hone your focus. Add speed, timing, strategy, surprise. Do not forget the Force is with you.|Another lesson from Jinn|<ref name="JA13" />}}
[[File:QuiGonJinnsLightsaber-TPM.png|thumb|250px|[[Qui-Gon Jinn's lightsaber/Legends|Qui-Gon Jinn's lightsaber]]]]
Qui-Gon Jinn, from a young age, exhibited promising talent in [[Lightsaber combat/Legends|lightsaber combat]] while still a mere trainee. He proved his skills during a lightsaber tournament held in the Exhibition Day, in which he made short work of all his opponents and ultimately bested Tahl in the final round, impressing many Jedi Masters and Dooku, one of the greatest lightsaber duelists in the Order, was impressed enough to take Jinn in as his Padawan. Refining his skills under Dooku's tutelage, Jinn became one of the Order's finest duelists, and he could easily defeat many enemies and he frequently sparred with many of his skilled contemporaries: his mentor, Dooku;<ref name="ROTS novel" /> Mace Windu, the creator of [[Form VII/Legends|Vaapad]];<ref name="NEGTC" /> and [[Jedi Weapon Master]] [[Anoon Bondara]].<ref name="Power of the Jedi">''[[Power of the Jedi Sourcebook]]''</ref> He also fought Xanatos always to a draw and even once managed to defeat him, wounding him in the shoulder and disarming him of Kenobi's lightsaber. Jinn was also able to battle Darth Maul, matching Maul long enough to escape unharmed in their first duel despite growing steadily tired and putting up a fight for a while despite being heavily fatigued and disadvantaged by Maul's knowledge of Jinn's fighting style before being finally struck down.

Jinn was incredibly skilled in the fourth form of lightsaber combat, [[Form IV/Legends|Form IV/Ataru]], being considered one of the greatest masters of the form among the Jedi. In combat, his bladework was wide and powerful, marked by heavy, two-handed slashes and sudden flourishes to cover his flanks. Jinn's mastery of Ataru was such that he could easily defeat blaster-wielding opponents despite the form's weakness to blaster fire. Rather than engaging in the energetic acrobatics typical of most Ataru specialists, Jinn, at least in his later years, tended to stay grounded during lightsaber duels.<ref name="The Phantom Menace" /> That being said, he remained fully capable of utilizing acrobatic attacks and maneuvers during combat.<ref name="JA8" /> Jinn was also capable of effectively employing unarmed combat strikes into his lightsaber sequences.<ref name="The Phantom Menace" /> During the Naboo crisis, Darth Plagueis felt that a whole ship of droids would be confounded and unable to stop him.<ref name="Darth Plagueis" />

However, Jinn was not without his weaknesses. Dooku had sparred with him plenty of times and knew every single flaw in the Ataru form.<ref name="ROTS novel" /> In his elder years, Jinn's strength and physical ability began to diminish from age, and his primary edge was derived from his experience and intuition rather than from his physical attributes. His flagging stamina became a particularly notable issue due to his practice of Ataru, an incredibly tiring combat form even under ideal circumstances.<ref name="TPM novel" /> Despite his mastery of Ataru, Jinn was still prey to some of the form's flaws, namely the weak defense and the lack of effectiveness in confined spaces.<ref name="TFUn" /><ref name="SW.com Fightsaber">{{SWArchive|url=games/videogames/news20080728.html|text=Fightsaber: Mastering the Art of Lightsaber Combat}}</ref> All these weaknesses came into play during his final duel against Darth Maul. During the duel, Jinn saw an opportunity to redirect the duel to a small melting pit room in the Naboo power core. Jinn hoped to use the confined space to prevent Maul from bringing his saberstaff to bear, giving himself the advantage. However, Maul was aware of what Jinn was attempting to accomplish, and believed that the negative effects that a small space would have on his own technique were negligible compared to the effects it would have on Jinn's. Maul allowed himself to be pushed into the melting pit room, and there, Jinn's strategy backfired as Maul had hoped it would. Closed in, forced onto the defensive, and heavily fatigued from the long duel leading up to this, Jinn was brought down.<ref name="TPM novel" /> These flaws in Jinn's technique were apparent enough that Maul reasoned out exactly how he could kill Jinn after less than a minute of being exposed to the Jedi Master's fighting style.<ref name="Journal: Maul" /><ref name="Wrath" />

Ataru was not Jinn's only fighting style, and he had learned other forms of lightsaber combat, possibly to better handle the weaknesses of Form IV. Being apprenticed to Dooku, the most renowned fencer of the time, it is apparent that Jinn learned the classical dueling form of [[Form II/Legends|Form II/Makashi]] from his master and he was versed enough to effectively incorporate its maneuvers into his dueling style.<ref name="Lightsabers">''[[Star Wars: Lightsabers: A Guide to Weapons of the Force]]''</ref> Not only was Form II more effective against a single lightsaber-wielding opponent,<ref name="Kotor II">''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords]]''</ref> but it was also more grounded,<ref name="The Jedi Path" /> as demonstrated in Jinn's duels with Darth Maul. His knowledge was also good enough that he apparently taught Xanatos how to use Makashi. He seemed to have been well-trained in [[Form V/Legends|Form V/Shien]] and [[Form III/Legends|Form III/Soresu]], as he could easily handle blaster-wielding opponents.<ref name="The Phantom Menace" /> When he and Kenobi fought Taxer Sundown's hypnotized soldiers, who were wielding training lightsabers,<ref name="Last Stand on Ord Mantell 2" /> he displayed a level of mastery of [[Form I/Legends|Form I/Shii-Cho]] shared with [[Kit Fisto/Legends|Kit Fisto]], albeit at a lesser degree.<ref name="The Jedi Path" /><ref name="Lair of Grievous">{{TCW|Lair of Grievous}}</ref>

At one point during his training, Jinn tried using a [[Whip (weapon)|whip]], only to find that it "tangles easily."<ref name="The Jedi Path" /> Nonetheless, he had gained some knowledge on how to combat opponents armed with [[Lightwhip/Legends|lightwhips]], [[Vibrowhip/Legends|vibro-whips]], and other similar weapons.<ref name="JA11" />

During combat, Jinn preferred to adjust his technique based on the needs of the moment, rather than focusing on an overall strategy.<ref name="CoD" /> On Esseles, to conserve the diminishing charge in his lightsaber, he used his [[Liquid-cable launcher/Legends|grappling spike launcher]] to snare two battle droids and yanked them off their feet.<ref name="EP I Adv 1" />

===Force talents===
{{Quote|Remember, concentrate on the moment. Feel, don't think. Trust your instincts.|Jinn to Anakin Skywalker, minutes before the [[Boonta Eve Classic/Legends|Boonta Eve Classic]]|<ref name="The Phantom Menace" />}}
A philosophical warrior, Qui-Gon Jinn believed heavily in what he referred to as the "Living Force," a method of focusing on the moment rather than contemplating the Force in all its degrees.<ref name="The Phantom Menace" />

Jinn had considerable skill with [[Telekinesis/Legends|telekinesis]]: lifting people or objects,<ref name="Dreadnaughts of Rendili 1" /> dislodging enemies with a single Force Push,<ref name="The Phantom Menace" /> throwing objects onto a desired target, swerving a shooter's weapon hand out of range,<ref name="CoD" /> and dismantling droids.<ref name="TPM novel" /> During his mission to rescue Adi Gallia, he used a Saber Throw to dislodge a droid attached to a [[Turbolift/Legends|turbolift]] shaft.<ref name="EP I Adv 1" /> He also applied a meditative trance known as [[Serenity (trance)|Serenity]], granting him renewed strength and focus,<ref name="SECR">''[[Star Wars Roleplaying Game Saga Edition Core Rulebook]]''</ref> as seen during the momentary break in his final duel with Darth Maul.<ref name="The Phantom Menace" />

Jinn was exceptionally skilled in mind tricks, as was evident when he knocked out Jar Jar and convinced Boss Nass to lend him, Obi-Wan Kenobi, and Jar Jar Binks a transport to Theed.<ref name="The Phantom Menace" /> An extraordinary account of his using this power was when he persuaded a Hutt guard working for Offworld to give him access to Xanatos' [[Xanatos's private office|private office]] on Bandomeer&mdash;a truly remarkable feat,<ref name="JA2" /> as the Hutt species possessed a level of natural resistance to Force suggestion that bordered on immunity.<ref name="Darth Plagueis" /> During the [[Battle for Alaris Prime]], he used the little-understood [[Jedi Concentration]] to take over a Trade Federation building.<ref name="Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds">''[[Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds]]''</ref> He was able to receive Force visions,<ref name="JA1" /><ref name="JA14" /><ref name="JA9" /> despite his preference to focus on the present rather than the future.<ref name="The Phantom Menace" /> In addition, he had some knowledge of Force healing,<ref name="JA1" /><ref name="JA12" /> as displayed in his futile attempt to save Tahl moments before her death.<ref name="JA15" />

One of Jinn's lesser known Force powers was [[Animal bond|animal friendship]]. On the unknown blue planet, he controlled the mind of a draigon and rode on its back for as long as he needed until he reached his destination.<ref name="JA1" /> Later, he took a mental hold on a [[kudana]] during his and Kenobi's mission on Rutan.<ref name="JA10" />

When a blind Tahl improved her other senses, Jinn was [[Magnify Senses|inspired to do the same]]. On Kegan, he used his sense of smell to help him and Adi Gallia slip out of the [[Gathering Circle]] unnoticed.<ref name="JA9" /> He could also [[Breath control|control his breathing]] for a considerable amount of time; he would be able to render himself immune to various [[Poison/Legends|poisons]],<ref name="The Phantom Menace" /> as well as remain still and [[Force cloak|hide his life signature]] from [[Probe droid/Legends|probe droids]].<ref name="JA14" /> Jinn could [[Tapas|warm himself with the Force]].<ref name="CoD" /> He was unable to sense that [[Darth Plagueis/Legends|Hego Damask]] was a Sith, thinking that the Muun was just a money-man, though the Sith Lord was afraid that Jinn and Kenobi together might sense he and Palpatine were darksiders if both Sith and Jedi were together, such as to talk to Padme.<ref name="Darth Plagueis" />

Due to Jinn's belief in the Living Force, he studied the ability to retain his consciousness after death and managed to achieve an incomplete mastery, able to become a [[Force ghost/Legends|Force ghost]] after he died at the hands of Maul, but he was not able to visually manifest himself and could only speak to others.

===Other skills===
When Dooku took Qui-Gon Jinn as his Padawan, he noted the boy's mind as "excellent," able to collect data and catalog them for a conclusion in less than a minute. This would serve Jinn well in future missions.<ref name="LotJ" />

Jinn had a vast knowledge of the architecture of many capital ships and large transports, and understood their abilities and vulnerable points, including the engineering and structure of the Trade Federation's landing craft. Because of this knowledge, both he and Kenobi were able to sneak onto separate ships and stow away until they reached the swamps of Naboo.<ref name="Obi-Wan game" /> He also exceeded Dooku in repairs, which his then-mentor acknowledged.<ref name="LotJ" />

While he usually let Kenobi handle driving a transport as the Padawan got older,<ref name="The Phantom Menace" /><ref name="CoD" /> Jinn did have some skill in piloting various speeders and every type of flying craft.<ref name="JA4" /> He drove an [[Hydrocraft|Agri-Corps boat]] and an Offworld [[Landspeeder/Legends|landspeeder]] during his time on Bandomeer.<ref name="JA2" /> His first time with a [[Swoop/Legends|swoop]] had been difficult, but he quickly managed to control it.<ref name="JA4" /> He later flew a [[Galan starfighter]] while bringing Tahl back to Coruscant to recuperate after their mission on Melida/Daan.<ref name="JA5" /> On his second mission to Telos, he navigated a [[Hoversled/Legends|gravsled]] to prevent Xanatos from escaping.<ref name="JA8" /> On Rutan, he briefly took the controls of Prince Taroon's transport to land them and Kenobi safely as the nervous young Rutanian shook the ship.<ref name="JA10" />

Jinn's linguistic capabilities were also notable. He was fluent in many languages, including [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Basic]], [[Nelvaanese]], [[Cerean (language)|Cerean]], [[Gran (language)/Legends|Gran]] and [[Shyriiwook/Legends|Shyriiwook]].<ref name="TFISWT(M)">''{{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/article/sw20050519a|text=The Force Is With Them (Mostly)}}''</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
===Portrayal===
{{Quote|He's almost like a monk, an old-time warrior who is wise and quite philosophical, yet very skilled in martial arts. He has incredible confidence, as well as a magical quality that enables him to see into the future. He's not really a rebel, but he has his own code.|Liam Neeson's thoughts on his character, Qui-Gon Jinn|<ref name="Star Wars: The Making of Episode I The Phantom Menace">''[[Star Wars: The Making of Episode I The Phantom Menace]]''</ref>}}
[[File:Qui-Gon_Jinn_Concept_Art.jpg|thumb|140px|Concept art of Liam Neeson as Jinn in ''The Phantom Menace'']]

Qui-Gon Jinn was portrayed by [[Liam Neeson]] in [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'']]. As revealed in ''[[The Art of Star Wars Episode I: The Phantom Menace]]'', [[George Lucas]] conceived Jinn's character during pre-production of ''The Phantom Menace''. This is shown by concept art where Kenobi is shown alone in the Federation ship and while meeting Binks. Even when Jinn was conceived, Lucas toyed with making him the younger Jedi, as shown in concept art depicting Kenobi as an old man.

Neeson's voice was later used briefly in [[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones|''Star Wars'': Episode II ''Attack of the Clones'']]. The character was voiced by [[Fred Tatasciore]] for the [[Star Wars: Clone Wars|''Star Wars: Clone Wars'' animated series]]. [[James Warwick]] voiced Qui-Gon Jinn in the [[1999]] [[Star Wars video games|video game]] [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace (video game)|adaptation of ''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'']], the [[2000]] video game ''[[Star Wars: Episode I Jedi Power Battles]]'', the [[2001]] video game [[Star Wars: Obi-Wan (video game)|''Star Wars: Obi-Wan'']] and the 2001 video game ''[[Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds]]''.

Jinn's voice was set to appear in [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith|''Revenge of the Sith'']], and Neeson had hinted at involvement in early 2005.<ref name="USA Today">{{WebCite|url=http://usatoday30.usatoday.com/life/people/2005-01-09-palm-springs_x.htm|text=Movie-star night in Palm Springs|author=Keck, William|date=2005-01-09|archivedate=20190901164001}}</ref> The scene was cut, however, and Neeson was never recorded.<ref name="Rick">{{SWBoards|url=thread.jspa?threadID=224485|thread=Star Wars: Message Boards: Rick McCallum|user=Rick McCallum|date=2005-03-06|time=4:00 PM|nobackup=1}}</ref> The scene between Yoda and Jinn can still be read in the film's screenplay and [[Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith (novelization)|the novelization]]. Jinn was also mentioned in the video game platform and Gameboy Advance/Nintendo DS versions of the [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith (video game)|''Revenge of the Sith'' game]].

Neeson reprised his role in [[2011]], voicing a ghostly Qui-Gon Jinn in ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]''.<ref name="insidetv">{{WebCite|url=https://ew.com/article/2011/01/20/liam-neeson-star-wars-clone-wars-exclusive|text=Liam Neeson to voice Qui-Gon Jinn in 'Star Wars: The Clone Wars'|author=Blauvelt, Christian|date=2011-01-20|archivedate=20200626195055}}</ref>

===Continuity===
There was some confusion as to how many apprentices Jinn had during the course of his career. All sources agree that he trained Xanatos and then Kenobi, but there is also the occasional reference to a Padawan before Xanatos. This discrepancy was solved in Jinn's Databank entry, which stated that "Qui-Gon obsessed over his failure for years, dismissing his earlier successes as a teacher and often referring to Xanatos as his 'first' apprentice."<ref name="Databank" /> In [[2011]], Jinn's first Padawan was identified as Feemor in the [[Star Wars: Jedi — The Dark Side|''Star Wars: Jedi—The Dark Side'']] comic series.

====Video games====
Qui-Gon Jinn has been featured in a number of video games set during the events of Episode I, some of which contradict the movie. This section describes the games and the contradictory elements presented in them.

=====''Star Wars: Jedi Power Battles''=====
The video game ''Star Wars: Episode I Jedi Power Battles'', which can be played with one or two players, featured Jinn as one of five playable characters. As the game takes place during the events of ''The Phantom Menace'', this article assumes that the two playable characters are Jinn and Kenobi. The levels ''Trade Federation Battleship'', ''Swamps of Naboo'', ''City of Theed'', and ''Theed Royal Palace'' take place from the start of the movie to the Jedi's departure on Theed. The first mission starts just after Jinn's and Kenobi's escape from the conference room aboard the Trade Federation flagship. They travel through the corridors and engage a large group of battle droids before finding a command center. They then travel on a conveyor to a hangar and duel a Cargo Loader Droid. They then continue through the ship and duel a droid starfighter. The next mission takes place in Naboo's swamps, after the Jedi meet Binks.

They escort the Gungan through the swamps and face a large group of battle droids throughout the mission. The level ends after defeating the Slaatik hagworm. If they take too long during the mission, Binks may be killed, although he runs off to the side and is hardly seen. The next mission takes place after the Jedi's arrival in Theed. The Jedi travel through the streets to the Palace; along the way they rescue several handmaidens from the droid. The mission requires the player to rescue seven of the handmaidens. During the mission the players take control of an Armored Assault Tank and use it to blast other tanks. They then dismount and destroy a T4 turret droid. The last mission in Theed contradicts the movie. The two Jedi infiltrate the Palace and fight through more battle droids. They then find a tomb, which opens to reveal one of the handmaidens they had rescued. She leads them to the Throne Room, where they rescue Queen Amidala from battle droids. They then escort her through the Palace to the Hangar, which is guarded by Plasma battle droids. This article assumes the second half of the mission is [[Canon|non-canon]].

In the ''Coruscant'' mission, the player(s) travel to the Jedi Temple while fighting gang members. The next mission, ''Ruins'', expands on the scene where the Queen and Jedi return to Theed. The player(s) fight through the swamps and some ruins before meeting the Gungan Security Chief. The next two missions feature a return to Theed: ''Streets of Theed'' puts the Jedi on captured Federation STAPs to travel to the Theed Royal Palace. In ''Palace Cliffs'', the player(s) scale the Palace cliffs and face five rooms out of six full of various types of battle droids to rescue Security Force pilots. The third chronicles the duel with Darth Maul. The duel in the game contradicts the movie, so this article does not incorporate its events.

The duel features extra posturing on Darth Maul's part, with him bowing twice to the player. They then duel, heading out of the hangar and into the power chamber. The player chases Maul around the catwalks and duels him on an energy bridge, before leaping down a set of rings and dueling Maul on the central catwalk. Maul Force-jumps away from the player, who chases the Sith Lord. In the next section, they face three battle droids and take an elevator up. On the upper catwalk, the player faces two more droids and must jump across a series of gaps which feature oscillating lasers. Once past, the player must disable two fans. They then disable a third fan and start jumping down its five levels, disabling more fans on the way down. The player ends up on the bottom of the power chamber and must avoid falling into the pool. Past that is a laser gate maze, which is guarded by more droids. The next section past the maze is a series of gaps which the player must jump over, while also avoiding the lasers. Once across, there is a short duel with Maul which is similar to the movie. If Jinn is a playable character, he can beat Darth Maul outright and appear in the victory celebration after the invasion was over. This article assumes the last mission is non-canonical.

=====''The Phantom Menace'' video game=====
Jinn is a playable character during the Tatooine portions (''Mos Espa'', ''Mos Espa Arena'' and ''Desert Encounter'') of the ''Star Wars Episode I: The Phantom Menace'' video game, which contradicts the movie in several places. He also appears in other missions supporting the player.

The game outright contradicts the movie scene during the mission ''Otoh Gunga''. In the game, Binks is arrested and separated from the Jedi, and Jinn orders Kenobi to travel through the city and rescue him. Kenobi travels through the city, [[Telekinesis/Legends#Force push|Force pushing]] guards out of his way and using a mind trick to secure the release of Binks. They then meet up with Jinn in the bongo transport bay. In the movie, Binks stands with them the whole scene.

In the game, the deal between Watto and Jinn is also changed, as Watto demands that Jinn pay him [[peggat]]s as an additional condition. Searching for the way to obtain the money, Jinn goes to Jabba the Hutt's quarters shortly before the podrace, where he fights a creature called [[Jabba's champion]]. Jinn defeats the beast and is given the peggats as a reward, which he uses to place a bet with Watto.

Because they directly contradict the film, this article assumes those scenarios to be non-canon.

=====Other Episode I video games=====
Jinn supports the player in [[Star Wars: Obi-Wan (video game)|''Star Wars: Obi-Wan'']], who takes the role of the titular Jedi in each mission. In the mission ''Betrayal'', Jinn and Kenobi escape from the Federation conference room and travel through the flagship until reaching the bridge. In that game they discover the invasion fleet before they do in the movie. Jinn's duel with Darth Maul at the start of the ''Darth Maul'' level is not scripted, and the player can see a different duel each time.

In ''Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds'', Jinn narrates the training campaign and appears throughout the game. The game requires Jinn to survive to complete the missions he appears in.

====Non-canon content====
Qui-Gon Jinn appeared in ''[[LEGO Star Wars: The Video Game]]'', which adapted the events of Episode I in a humorous fashion. He later appeared in ''[[LEGO Star Wars II: The Original Trilogy]]'' as an unlockable character and in the compilation of the two games, titled ''[[LEGO Star Wars: The Complete Saga]]''. He later made another appearance as an unlockable character in ''[[LEGO Star Wars III: The Clone Wars]]''.

In the [[2008]] [[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed|''Star Wars: The Force Unleashed'' video game]], a player who enters MAVERICK as a cheat code can play as Qui-Gon Jinn. In the [[Wikipedia:PlayStation Portable|PSP]] duel mode of the game, Qui-Gon Jinn fights the player along with Obi-Wan. Jinn is also a playable character in the expansion pack ''[[Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds: Clone Campaigns]]''.

Jinn appears as a disembodied voice in the non-canon comic ''[[Star Wars: Visions of the Blade]]'', a prequel to the fighting game ''[[Soulcalibur IV]]'', which features ''Star Wars'' characters. In the comic, Yoda, while in exile on Dagobah, experiences a vision of [[Astaroth]] approaching the sword [[Soul Edge]]. Jinn contacts Yoda, encouraging him to temporarily step out of his exile and set out to the [[Cowl Crucible]] to confront the enemy.

In the [[Star Wars Infinities: A New Hope 3|third issue]] of the comic series ''[[Star Wars Infinities: A New Hope]]'', in which the Rebel Alliance failed to destroy the Death Star and lost the Battle of Yavin, Luke Skywalker goes to train with Yoda on Dagobah. While inside the [[Cave of Evil/Legends|Dark Side cave]], he experiences a number of visions, including that of Jinn stating that he has "encountered a vergence in The Force". In another alternate storyline, ''[[Star Wars Infinities: The Empire Strikes Back]]'', Skywalker freezes to death on Hoth, leaving Leia to go to Dagobah and train as a Jedi. After she has left the planet, Darth Vader arrives there and confronts Yoda. The two engage in battle of the minds, in which Vader is attacked by the spirits of Jedi from his past, including Jinn.
